articleTitle: Development of an Algorithm for Generating an OCDM-OChDM Signal
abstract: In this publication, we have developed an Orthogonal Code Division Multiplexing - Orthogonal Chirp Division Multiplexing signal-code construction to improve the noise immunity of a signal in the channel with Additive white Gaussian noise. The noise immunity of the proposed construction is compared with the results obtained for the Orthogonal Code Division Multiplexing - Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing signal implemented in the article by Karpukhin and Makarenkov for various orthogonal code sequences.

articleTitle: Beamforming and Direction of Arrival Estimation for Beam Management in 5G mmWave UDN
abstract: The distinctive feature of 5G ultra-dense networks (UDN), compared with mobile networks of previous generations, is more widespread utilization of beamforming (BF) and direction of arrival (DOA) estimation techniques, which require prompt and effective beam management (BM) procedures. High density of gNodeB (gNB) and User Equipment (UE) distribution even up to one device per square meter leads to prevalent line-of sight (LOS) conditions on the one hand and huge level of intra-system interference with difficultly predictable signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) on the other hand. To support acceptable SINR level in 5G UDN we propose to use BF and DOA estimation for beam management. Contribution of current research is simulation of a spatial separation of UE based on beam management and three-dimensional BF using adaptive antenna arrays with preliminary DOA estimation.

articleTitle: Software-Defined Radio Network Positioning Technology Design. MIB Transceiver Development
abstract: The problem of positioning of user equipment (UE) using LTE mobile communication network has become highly relevant in recent years, especially for GNSS denied environment. The object of this research is a software-defined radio (SDR) LTE network positioning technology prototype design for testing new technical solutions to improve the accuracy of UE location estimation in existing LTE and emerging 5G NR networks. Correct functioning UE during reception of reference signals for positioning purpose requires processing of various control signal information blocks, transmitted by the eNodeB. The purpose of this research is development and validation of the Master Information Block (MIB) transmission and reception for bandwidth acquisition on-the-fly during UE positioning in LTE network. The contribution of this research is MIB software realization and its experimental validation in laboratory conditions.

articleTitle: An Effective Post - Filtering for Minimum Variance Distortionless Response Beamformer
abstract: An effective hands-free speech interface with an appropriate digital signal processing is essential for teleconference systems and control systems. Beamforming technique, which use a microphone array (MA) is an ideal solution for distant - talking speech acquisition, is one of the most attractive approaches for suppressing background noise and improving the speech intelligibility and speech quality of the processing system. Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) has the capacity of maximizing the sensitivity in a certain direction at aiming to extract the desired target speech while removing all total power of surrounding noise. However, in many complex recording environments, due to the error of direction of arrival of interest speaker, the difference of microphone sensitivities, imprecise designed geometry of MA, the performance of MVDR beamformer often degraded. In this contribution, the authors suggested an additive post-filtering to enhance the effectiveness of MVDR beamformer.

articleTitle: The Scheme of an Expert System for Processing Multispectral Information from an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: Nowadays, the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (further on referred to as UAV) is a promising way to diagnose power grid elements. Replacing the currently used teams of workers with the above-mentioned method will make it possible to solve the problems of finding and eliminating defects much faster and more accurately on such extended and difficult-to-reach electric power facilities as power lines. Obtaining more extensive information about defects requires installing sensors of various spectra on board UAV: visible, infrared and ultraviolet. The expert system based on artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies should be used to process multispectral information. The expert system (further on referred to as ES) is a complex of hardware and software installed both on the UAV and on the operator's devices, from which the flight is controlled and information is received. The scheme and principles of this system operation will be discussed in the article.

articleTitle: Synthesis of a Tunable Band-Stop Filter
abstract: Tunable band-stop filters are important for selective conversion of electrical signals in radio technical devices and systems, in equalizers for the noise suppression, in measuring complexes, in acoustic and hydroacoustic equipment, etc. These filters are usually complex due to a large number of amplifiers and passive elements. The implementation of tunable active RC filters with several operational amplifiers ensures the improved filters characteristics and low sensitivity of the basic parameters of filters to scattering of electrical elements values. The active RC filter, which is characterized by independent tuning within the wide limits of a resonance frequency, quality factor and transmission coefficient, is presented. The resonance frequency of the tunable band-stop filter is adjusted with the aid of a potentiometer with the maintenance of the transmission coefficient and small changes in the pole quality factor of a transfer function. The pole quality factor and transmission coefficient are independently adjusted by means of two variable resistors. The properties of the represented tunable band-stop filter provide high technological efficiency and convenient manner of the operating modes tuning.

articleTitle: Increasing the Speed of Wavelet Image Processing with Decimation Using the Winograd Method
abstract: Wavelet processing is actively used for image de noising, compression, and fusion. The high growth rate of quantitative and qualitative characteristics of digital images, lead to the need to increase the speed of wavelet image processing methods and their efficient implementation on modern hardware devices. This paper proposes the Winograd method (WM) to speed up the wavelet image processing methods due to group pixel processing. The scheme of wavelet filtering of images using WM with decimation has been developed. The proposed approach reduced the asymptotic computational complexity of wavelet transform up to 53 % compared to the pixel-by-pixel processing. Estimating the time spent on a hardware device based on a unit-gate model showed that WM reduces device delay up to 67% compared to the direct method. The proposed approach implementation of wavelet image processing on a field-programmable gate arrays and an application-specific integrated circuits is a promising direction for further research.

articleTitle: Analysis of Signals Detection Methods Using Image Processing
abstract: Algorithms for multisignals detection using image processing are investigated. Approaches based on digital image processing, as well as on the use of neural networks and deep learning are considered. A comparative analysis of the listed methods for their further application in the detection of FHSS-signals from the spectrogram image is given.

articleTitle: A Method for Optimizing the Optical Parameters of an Orbital Computer Cision System to Increase the Efficiency of Space Debris Monitoring
abstract: The article proposes a method for evaluating the effectiveness of space debris monitoring by an orbital computer vision system. The search for the optimal angle of the field of view at a fixed aperture number is carried out, and the optimal sensor-lens configurations are analyzed, at which the number of detected objects is maximum. A pronounced optimum was found at field of view angles from 35 to 45 degrees.

articleTitle: Air Navigation: Improving the Quality of Radar Surveillance Systems
abstract: It is shown that for a joint radar as part of the primary, secondary and identification radar stations, a significant impact on the integral quality indicator is exerted by the readiness factor of the transponders of the secondary radars, which can be con-trolled by the concerned party by setting correlated interference, which is very dangerous, and on the signal-to-noise ratio of the primary radar.

articleTitle: Descriptive Analysis and Acoustic Emission Signals Parameters Assessments: Signal Processing Data
abstract: This article presents the results of processing full-scale acoustic emission signals obtained at selective laser melting (SLM) process. During the recording of acoustic emission signals during the SLM process, electrical noise and continuous noise arise. For filtering these noises, their frequencies are identified. Noise suppression was carried out on the basis of the previously developed and proposed method for filtering the acoustic emission signal. The scheme of bi-directional filtering and their convolution in the frequency domain is presented. An increase in the efficiency of acoustic emission signal processing has been established. Descriptive analysis of the results before and after filtering the signal parameter shows a statistically significant difference. This difference characterizes the increase in the information content of the measurement results.

articleTitle: Raw Data Point Cloud Probabilistic Filtering Algorithm
abstract: Solving the problem of detecting a moving object in a video stream in real time is one of the urgent tasks in computer vision systems. There are various ways, methods and computational algorithms for solving it. One of the promising algorithms for detecting and predicting the position of a moving object is the probabilistic Kalman filter. On the other hand, to detect a moving object and determine the distance to it, the approach of merging lidar and camera sensors is increasingly used. The Kalman filter can be applied as a suitable filtering algorithm capable of handling multiple inputs. This paper proposes a filtering algorithm based on the integration of probabilistic and median data filtering. The advantage of this approach is the replacement of the division operation in computational calculations by the Goldschmidt algorithm. The developed algorithm will reduce the delay time of the algorithm, as well as improve its accuracy. The results obtained can be effectively applied in various computer vision systems.

articleTitle: Modern Trends in Hyperspectral Archival Document Image Processing: a Review
abstract: Archival documents are susceptible to degradation, resulting in the loss of information, which often has cultural and heritage value. Hyperspectral processing is one of the effective information recovery methods for archival documents, moreover, it can be used for documents imaging analysis. This approach allows you to restore documents from breaks and stains, to increase visibility, as well as analyze them, the purpose of which can be ink classification, text erasure analysis or artworks authentication. This paper focuses on the analytical review of modern hyperspectral methods that are used to solve processing and analyzing archival documents and printed publications tasks.

articleTitle: LoRa Based Transceiver for Arctic Region
abstract: The difficult climatic conditions of regions of the far north determine the necessity for the development of special information transmission devices. This paper is devoted to the development of transceiver based on LoRa technology for use in the Arctic region. Attention is focused on the significance of the distinctive features of these devices, which are low power consumption, small overall dimensions and light weight, autonomy and portability. Various variants of passive antennas are considered, including whip, helical, bidquad antennas. The maximum signal transmission distance is estimated when sending text messages. Also RSSI and SNR are estimated.

articleTitle: Applications of the Adaptive Filtering Algorithm for Ultra-high Resolution Electrocardiosignals
abstract: The development and implementation of a new proprietary method of ultra-high resolution electrocardiography (UHR ECG) is based on the development of procedures for digital processing of recorded ultra-high resolution electrocardiosignals (UHR ECS). It is the digital processing of these weak signals, including digital filtering, that determines the possibility of studying the fine structure of micropotentials that carry diagnostic information about the development or absence of the studied pathologies of the cardiovascular system at earlier stages of their development. It is known that during electrocardiographic studies, electrocardiographic signals are affected by various interferences caused by external power sources, magnetic field, and internal noise of the recording device. The paper presents the use of a special adaptive algorithm for filtering the UHR ECS, which allows processing the data under study using records of the idling of the recording device. The efficiency of the presented algorithm was evaluated by such parameters as mean square error (MSE) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). In addition, a comparison is made between the proposed adaptive algorithm and a comb digital filter.

articleTitle: Method of Refining the Determination of the Frequency of Monoharmonic Signal Using a Discrete Fourier Transform
abstract: The paper demonstrates the possibility of increasing the accuracy of determining the frequency by the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) algorithm without invoking any additional information. To do this it is sufficiently more efficient to use a priori information and information contained in the output message of the DFT.

articleTitle: Spectral Mask - Based Technique for Improving Generalized Sidelobe Canceller Beamformer's Evaluation
abstract: Noise suppression and understanding speech in a complex environment with the presence of numerous and dominant surrounding noise is very difficult for humans. To deal with this problem, microphone array, which exploit a priori information of designed geometry of microphone array, the direction of arrival (DOA) of interest signal or the properties of recorded situation, is used with aiming at preserving the desired speaker without speech distortion while reducing background noise. Generalized Sidelobe Canceller (GSC) beamformer has been installed in almost all acoustic equipment, hearing aids, mobile phones. Unfortunately, the performance of GSC beamformer is often corrupted in many scenarios, such as imprecise DOA, microphone mismatches or different microphone sensitivities. In this paper, a spectral mask - based suggested algorithm to reduce the speech leakage in the reference signal of GSC beamformer. The proposed method is evaluated for increasing the speech quality of dual - microphone systems.

articleTitle: A Method for Reducing Speech Distortion in Minimum Variance Distortionless Response Beamformer
abstract: Speech processing devices such as mobile telephone, hearing aid, cochlear implant is commonly equipped with a designed microphone array (MA) to capture the acoustic environment. The MA signals often contain a mixture of desired speech component and unwanted surrounding noise (a combination of reverberation, different interferences, complex recording environment, third-party speaker). Minimum Distortionless Variance Response (MVDR) beamformer is one the most useful methods for reducing background noise and improving speech enhancement has been recently studied. MVDR beamformer merges the predefined constraints of response from a priori relative transfer function and the criteria of minimum total output noise power. Because of the microphone mismatches, the different microphone sensitivities, or the error of the direction of arrival of the interest signal, the output final signal of MVDR beamformer often corrupted. In this paper, the authors proposed an additive gain function for reducing speech distortion and enhancing MVDR beamformer's performance.

articleTitle: Solving Poisson Equation by Physics-Informed Neural Network with Natural Gradient Descent with Momentum
abstract: In this paper, we present a solution of the first boundary value problem of the Poisson equation using physics-informed neural networks, which optimize the loss function by natural gradient descent with Dirichlet distribution. This algorithm proved his ability in optimization of multidimensional functions with high accuracy, taking little number of iterations and avoiding local minimums. This fact means, that proposed algorithm will minimize loss function as well. Also, we obtain the exact and numerical solutions, implied due to separation of variable (Fourier method) and finite element method, respectively. The main goal of this paper is to rise the accuracy of solution of the Poisson equation in a short time. We will demonstrate the error estimate of solutions received by finite element method and physics-informed neural network, equipped with adaptive moment estimates and natural gradient descent with momentum and Nesterov condition.

articleTitle: Non-parametric Bayesian Network for Surrogate Data
abstract: In recent years, domain experts indicated increasing interest in Bayesian Networks (BN). BN can be represented by a directed acyclic graph, the nodes of which, corresponding to the random variables under study, are connected by edges representing direct relationship between the nodes. For the unknown distributions of the analyzed variables, non-parametric Bayesian networks (NPBN) are used to build a graphical probabilistic model. The current study focuses on the application of MATLAB toolbox BANSHEE for creating NPBN for a set of surrogate random variables with certain cross-correlation coefficients. An acyclic directed graph was constructed, in which links between parent and child nodes were established based on expert assessment. Gaussian copula based on the Spearman's rank correlation was considered as a metric of interrelation between two connected nodes. Two diagnostic tests were carried out for the constructed NPBN. The Cramer-von Mises test showed that the Gaussian copula represents an effective solution for the characterization of all pairwise interactions between variables. Calculation of the d- calibration score confirmed that the Gaussian copula matches the proposed BN structure.

articleTitle: Bit Error Rate Analysis of Time Domain Low Rank Channel Precoder in M-MIMO Systems
abstract: In this paper we proposed the evaluated bit error rate (BER) performance of wireless channel beam-forming technology in wideband precoder manner. We focused on massive multiple-input multiple-output (M-MIMO) mobile system with extended antenna number on transmission side and receiver user equipment (UE) side. Basically, the channel precoding processing provide in frequency domain, in OFDM- MIMO system jointly. For computational complexity reduction of beam-forming processing for each sub-band we calculate the precoder in time-domain by 1D-DFT approximation in frequency domain for 1st layer transmission. For reliability estimation of received data on UE we analysis the performance of BER vs SNR through frequency-selective MIMO channel under A WNG condition. In the end of paper, we make sure that the processing in the OFDM system of precoder recalculation in time-domain achieve a gain in energy efficiency term, approximately 1–2 dB, compared with PSK modulation scheme, and losses less than 10% compared with baseline beam-forming algorithm in frequency-domain.

articleTitle: Classification of Fault Signals by Chaotic Oscillators Synchronization
abstract: Among ways of technical systems monitoring, methods using sensors of mechanical vibrations are widely used. Such sensors make it possible to inspect vibrations in electrical machines, gearboxes and other mechanisms and to identify signs of malfunctions. Simple and efficient algorithms for finding signs of faults, suitable for use in low-cost hardware, are in demand. One of the newest techniques in this field is the diagnostics based on chaotic systems. We propose a new method of this family based on the observing the synchronization error between two chaotic oscillators. For numerical study, recordings of vibrations of a motor with faulty bearing were used. We show that the proposed method reliably identifies the signs of a defect in the presence of background noise.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Assessing Cardiovascular Activity
abstract: This article describes an algorithmic complex for analyzing the parameters of the CVS and its activity. The undoubted advantage of this complex is the ability to analyze additional parameters of electrocardiograms and photoplethysmograms, such as blood pressure and cardiac output. The use of a large amount of additional diagnostic data, the use of modern algorithms, makes it possible to identify the risk of developing arterial hypertension (AH), as well as the possibility of developing heart failure. This article also includes a description of generally accepted signal processing algorithms. The effectiveness of application algorithms was evaluated using a verified database of signals and pathological forms. This article also presents an analysis of the main issues that appear when identifying the characteristic points of a pulse wave (PW) signal. To process synchronous recordings of pulse wave signals, blood pressure and electrocardiogram (ECG) in the Matlab environment, a software module has been developed that provides the possibility of synchronous signal construction, selection of characteristic points of these signals, calculation of parameters of cardiovascular activity, an indicator of the pulse wave propagation time and an assessment of its variability, calculation of stroke volume, as well as an assessment of the risk of developing heart failure.

articleTitle: Comparison of Adaptive Kalman Filters for Suppressing Random Noise of Optical Gyroscopes in Inertial Navigation
abstract: Random noise in optical gyroscopes (fiber optic, laser gyroscopes) will make the zero-offset or scale factor drift and unstable, that is a major factor causing errors in strapdown inertial navigation systems over time. In the last decade, many noise reduction methods and noise compensation algorithms have been developed. The most popular are random noise modeling methods combined with methods for their compensation based on adaptive Kalman filters. This paper summarizes, classifies, and compares the methods used over the last 15 years. Their advantages and disadvantages are pointed out, which is the basis for choosing a suitable option in a specific navigation task.

articleTitle: Improving the Efficiency of RF Spectrum Monitoring when Receiving Superimposed Pulses Based on an Adjustable Optical Delay Line
abstract: To conduct RF spectrum monitoring in conditions of pulse superposition, it is proposed to install a delay device at the input of the RF spectrum monitoring receiver. He principle of operation of the delay device consists of multiple signal transfers from the microwave range to the optical one and vice versa with the passage through fiber segments of various lengths. The purpose of the work is to substantiate and develop the operation algorithm for the delay device installed at the input of a matrix receiver to ensure the processing of time-overlapped pulses. The use of a delay device operating in accordance with the proposed algorithm makes it possible to reduce the likelihood of measurement ambiguity and anomalous errors during the operation of RF spectrum monitoring based on a matrix receiver under conditions of imposition of pulses in time.

articleTitle: Air Navigation: Data Support of Airspace Surveillance Systems in the Airport Area
abstract: The value of the analog signal detection threshold is used as a parameter in the joint optimization of observation data pro-cessing. To optimize the measurement of the state of the air-borne vehicles, it should be transmitted as part of the airborne vehicles form and the matrix of the accuracy of measuring the signal parameters and the coordinates of the airborne vehicles at the previous stage of information processing. Mathematical models have been developed for estimating the probability of a false alarm and the risk of the integrity and integrity of the co-ordinate information of broadcast automatic dependent surveil-lance based on a comparison of the radar station horizontal position marks from two independent radars. An algorithm has been developed to ensure the integrity of information for speech automatic dependent observation using the indicated models

articleTitle: Development of a Mathematical Model of the Receiving Path of the System, Registration of Ionizing Radiation
abstract: In this paper the mathematical model of the receiving path of the system, which registers ionizing radiation, is considered and its work is simulated. The model of ionizing radiation, scintillator and SiPM (device consisting of matrix of avalanche photodiodes) is described. Proposed, described and justified the model of registration of high-energy particles, taking into account characteristic noises. For each link of the path, the corresponding output characteristics were obtained, and then their composition was taken.

articleTitle: Application of Parametric Methods for the Synthesis of Directivity Characteristics in Two-Dimensional Antenna Arrays
abstract: The paper investigates directivity characteristics of the two-dimensional antenna array (AA) for a passive coherent radar (PCR) constructed using the modified parametric Burg method in the problem of single signal detection. A comparative analysis of the obtained directivity characteristics with the characteristics formed using traditional algorithms based on the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) is carried out. DFT beamforming algorithms are widespread for spatial signal processing in AAs with equidistant arrangement of antenna elements (AEs). However, violation of the AE equidistance, as well as the errors in estimating individual AE coordinates using local positioning systems, negatively affect the AA directivity characteristics and make the DFT algorithms impractical. Directivity characteristics for the comparative analysis were obtained using computer simulation in the MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model of the Signal Classification Algorithm with Detection at Two Intermediate Frequencies
abstract: A mathematical model of the signal classification algorithm by the type of intrapulse modulation is developed for RF spectrum sensing. Compared to the known ones, the algorithm makes it possible to determine more types of intrapulse modulation. This is provided by additional signal processing at two non-zero intermediate frequencies, one of which is doubled. The classification criteria are justified.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Influence of the Characteristics of Electrocardiogram Signals and Noises on the Effectiveness of the Classification of Human Body Conditions
abstract: The article examines the influence of the sampling frequency and the noise power of electrocardiosignals on the accuracy, specificity and sensitivity of the classification of states of the human body. To solve the classification problem, one of the types of artificial neural network (ANN) is used - a deep neural network (DNN). The result is the identification of dependencies of classification indicators on changes in signal characteristics.

articleTitle: Autofocusing Algorithm for Radar Images Obtained Under Severe Carrier Vehicle Motion Trajectory Instability
abstract: The majority of existing radar image autofocusing algorithms unable to provide high-quality images obtained under severe carrier vehicle motion traj ectory instability without using additional navigational information. This paper presented the radar images autofocusing algorithm, based on a seamless stitching of the image focused segments. For image segments focusing robust focus measure is used, which relies on radar image brightness and variance. Image segments shift and scale are determined by the usage of a correlational algorithm. In the final section, the application of the proposed algorithm on the actual radar data from an X-band synthetic aperture radar is described.

articleTitle: Tracking of Surface Maneuvering Targets Based on Interactive Multi-model Algorithm
abstract: Trajectory filtering is one of the important target tracking problems that has received attention in recent years. An interactive multi-model algorithm (IMM) is proposed for tracking maneuvering surface vessels. The simulation of the work of algorithms for trajectory filtering of targets in the Matlab environment is given. The next direction is suggested in the conclusion.

articleTitle: Low Entropy Signals in Electric Power System and Its Applications
abstract: The article deals with the property of low entropy of voltage and current in electric power systems. A formula is derived for determining the amount of information generated by electric power systems and the simulation results are discussed. The conclusion is made about the possibility of using the low entropy property to identify the states of electric power systems. Methods for improving the accuracy of measuring higher harmonics are presented. An increase in accuracy is achieved by eliminating the deterministic component from the measured signal. The possibility of analyzing the impact of an electromagnetic storm or the Northern Lights on power lines is being investigated. In this case, the low-frequency noise is separated from the low-frequency noise of the ADC using a special calibration algorithm. The problems of using FFT for low-entropy signals are studied. This problem is caused by the quasiperiodicity of electrical signals, which leads to the formation of a lattice spectrum and, accordingly, to a sharp increase in the measurement error when the FFT samples are shifted from the current and voltage harmonics.
